items.anchor: A finite algebraic cycle first determines every query of a specified line search.
items.note: Chapter summary (both sentences of line 3): the cycle (D:closure) and the trial tree for all pairs (prose/026) determine the queries; Theorem D:main gives the fixed convex objective with failing starts approaching the optimizer.

items.anchor: There is no resetting, damping, rescaling of the stored matrix, memory truncation, or skipped update.
items.note: Every run (AdmissibleBFGSRun) uses the full step and the full update ℬ(H_k,g_k,g_{k+1},α_k) at every step.

items.anchor: The line search is Algorithm 4.6 of Lewis--Overton
items.note: The specified search (brackets ℓ = 0, h = +∞, α = 1; Armijo first, weak Wolfe second; bisection or doubling) is DeterministicLineSearch.fromMetric; specified_search unfolds one step and shows that an exhausted budget is failure. The identification with Lewis-Overton's Algorithm 4.6 is a literature attribution (not formalized).

items.anchor: All decisions below are strict; using non-strict acceptance inequalities produces the identical orbit.
items.note: For the three runs of the chapter (on G, on Ḡ, and the runs of D:main) and every pair of the range: the non-strict search (NonStrictLineSearch) returns the same output as the strict one at every iterate, and every run of the non-strict implementation from the same initial point and matrix has the same iterates and matrices.

items.anchor: Every trial point, not just every accepted point, is differentiable.
The accepted lengths are not assigned externally.
Thus the construction resolves the implementation-selection issue.
items.reason: Remark on the construction: the accepted lengths are outputs of the specified search (disp/006); no further claim.
items.note: Wording point W7 applied on 15 October 2026. The clause "left open by the previous admissible-length counterexample", which had no antecedent in the companion (history of the source report), was dropped.

items.anchor: It does not address strong-Wolfe interpolation searches or a positive-measure basin of failing initial points.
items.note: A scope remark. Its mathematical content: the failing starts x₀^{(n)} = p_n + a_n²z₀, n ≥ 1, form a countable Lebesgue-null set (no positive-measure basin). Strong-Wolfe interpolation searches are outside the theorem (no claim).

items.anchor: Choose the unique root in the closed
items.note: Defines (c,d) = AlgebraicSeed.root = (seedC, seedD): it lies in the closed sup-norm box of radius 10^-30 around (c₀,d₀), solves D:polys, and is the only solution there (uniqueness: Lemma D:root).

items.anchor: The decimals here are exact terminating rationals defining the box, not replacements for the algebraic root.
items.reason: Remark on presentation: the box center is exactly the displayed decimals (BfgsCoverage.Article.SeedCertificate.center_def) and the root is defined by the equations (prose/009).

items.anchor: The uniquely active gradient at $z_j$ is $g_j$ for $j=0,1,2$, and $g_0$ at $z_3$.
The identity is not inferred from near-closure.
items.reason: Methodological remark (the closure is an exact identity, disp/021, not a numerical observation).

items.anchor: One way to derive the formulas is to write the middle update as $C+\beta D$.
items.note: Under the standing assumptions of the paragraph: ℬ(M₁,g₁,g₂,b) = C + bD for every b ≠ 0, with explicit C, D independent of b.

items.anchor: Requiring $(C+\beta D)g_2$ to be parallel to $g_0-g_2$ is linear in $\beta$.
items.note: With "Its solution is the formula above." The 2×2 determinant of (C+bD)g₂ and g₀−g₂ is affine in b with nonzero slope, and (C+bD)g₂ is a multiple of g₀−g₂ (parallel; g₀ ≠ g₂ since Y ≠ 0) exactly when b = 66048RK/(UV(U+129)).

items.anchor: and choose $\gamma$ so that the last displacement is $\widetilde\rho(g_0-g_2)$.
items.note: With "The last update then gives ρ̃I: its two projection factors are the orthogonal projector onto (g₀−g₂)^⊥." With γ of disp/020 the last displacement is ρ̃(g₀−g₂); the last update is ρ̃I; both factors I − syᵀ/(yᵀs), I − ysᵀ/(yᵀs) equal P = I − yyᵀ/(yᵀy), the orthogonal projector onto y^⊥ (P² = P, Pᵀ = P, Py = 0, Pw = w for w ⊥ y).

items.anchor: Equations~\eqref{D:polys} are exactly $\beta=1/4$ and $\gamma=1/16$.
items.note: Under the standing assumptions of the paragraph, each equation of D:polys is equivalent to the corresponding length condition.

items.anchor: This proves~\eqref{D:closure} and~\eqref{D:steps}.
items.note: At the root, β = 1/4, γ = 1/16 and ρ̃ = ρ (SeedCycle.source_parameters), so disp/021 and disp/023 give D:closure and D:steps.

items.anchor: The Lean formalization checks these exact identities from the actual full-BFGS formulas
items.note: A description of the formalization (software); its mathematics is stated: at the root, for each update of the cycle, positive curvature, the secant identity H₊y = s, the inverse of H₊ is the Hessian BFGS update of M_j⁻¹, M_j and H₊ positive definite; on the whole root box, M₀, M₁, M₂ and the last update positive definite and the three curvatures positive. The exact identities themselves are disp/015, disp/016, disp/021, disp/023.

items.note: Strict activity of the branch at each of the nine trial points (the first conjunct of trial_bounds, for the queries).

items.note: The accepted points z₁, z₂, z₃ (and the start z₀) satisfy the bounds of D:trialbounds (trial_bounds, points of Failure.seedPoint).

items.anchor: Every trial at the corresponding phase is exactly $\rho^m$ times its listed base trial.
items.note: With "All comparison quantities scale by ρ^m, preserving every decision, not only acceptance at the selected length." At the iterate 3m+j of the run on G, each trial point is ρ^m(z_j+αp_j), the direction is ρ^mp_j, function differences and gradient–direction products scale by ρ^m, and the strict Armijo and weak Wolfe tests decide as at the base point, for all constants.

items.anchor: Thus $x_k\to0$ and $G(x_k)\downarrow0$.
items.note: For the run on G: x_k → 0, G(x_k) > 0 strictly decreasing with limit 0.

items.anchor: This limit is nonstationary
In particular $G(td_*)=-t$ for $t\ge0$ and $0\notin\operatorname{conv}\{g_0,g_1,g_2\}$.
items.note: Stated with the range t ≥ 0 (the article's M9 does not recur).

items.anchor: All trial values of $G$ are positive while $v-17<0$
items.note: At every iterate and every trial point of the run: G > 0 and v − 17 < 0.

items.anchor: The fourth piece never affects the line search.
items.note: Ḡ = G at every iterate and trial point, and the strict search on Ḡ returns the same output as on G at every iterate (every 0 < c₁ ≤ 1/3, c₂ > 0).

items.anchor: The convex combination of branches $0,1,3$ with weights $(8/17,8/17,1/17)$ is identically $-1$.
Equality fixes the unique minimizer $(-1,16)$, and branch $2$ is strictly below $-1$ there.
Sublevels are bounded, because $u\le t$, $v\le t+17$, and $-u-v/8\le t$ give lower bounds on both coordinates.
items.note: On {Ḡ ≤ t}: u ≤ t, v ≤ t+17, −u−v/8 ≤ t, hence v ≥ −16t and u ≥ −t−(t+17)/8; the sublevel set is bounded.

items.anchor: This supplies a coercive deterministic failure
but does not alone refute local convergence at its true minimizer. The next construction does.
items.note: The first clause is a remark on scope (the run on Ḡ converges to 0, far from the minimizer (−1,16), so it is not a local failure at the minimizer); the second is Theorem D:main (starts approaching the minimizer of F).

items.anchor: Then $0\le P_b'\le96$ and $\int_0^1P_b(\xi)\,d\xi=1-c_b$.
These intervals cover the real line, with agreeing formulas at shared endpoints.
items.note: The intervals x < −1, [−1,0], [bϑa_n, ba_n] (n ≥ 0), x ≥ b cover ℝ; the formulas agree at the shared endpoints −1, ba_{n+1} = bϑa_n and b.

items.anchor: The construction even gives globally Lipschitz second derivatives.
items.note: φ_b'' is globally Lipschitz (constant max{6, 139264/(5b²)}); for the branches see prose/046.

items.anchor: The second derivative is continuous across every join and at the accumulation point $0$.
items.note: φ_b'' is continuous on ℝ.

items.anchor: The uniform bound above, together with the bound $6$ on the negative cubic part, proves global Lipschitz continuity of $\varphi_b''$ by summing over interval lengths.
items.note: On the negative cubic part −1 < x < 0, φ_b''' = −6; the global Lipschitz constant is max{6, 139264/(5b²)}.

items.anchor: Thus the branches below are in $C^{2,1}$ as well.
items.note: C² with globally Lipschitz Hessians (Euclidean operator norm against the Euclidean distance, constant 60000).

resolved_discrepancies.description: "Thus the branches below are in $C^{2,1}$ as well. This does not make them analytic or uniformly strongly convex." (12_D.tex:380). "Them" are the branches of the single objective F = max fᵢ of display D:fullobjective (12_D.tex:396-403): f₀(u,v) = φ₂(u), f₁(u,v) = φ₂(−u−v/8), f₂(u,v) = φ_{b*}(cu+dv), f₃(u,v) = v. The fourth branch is linear, hence analytic at every point (Lean counterexample: Companion.Ch12D.branch3_analytic), so the sentence is false for it. The rest is true (Lean: Companion.Ch12D.not_analytic): f₀, f₁, f₂ are not analytic on ℝ², because φ₂ and φ_{b*} are not (φ_b = −x³ on [−1,0], so an analytic φ_b would equal −x³ on ℝ by the identity theorem, but φ_b(b) = 1); and no branch fᵢ, i = 0,…,3, is uniformly strongly convex, because each is constant along a nonzero direction: for no μ > 0 is ∇²fᵢ ⪰ μI everywhere, fᵢ − (μ/2)‖·‖₂² convex, or fᵢ μ-strongly convex for the sup norm. The same wording issue as M8 (A/master/prose/009, A/verification/prose/017, A/lower_curvature/prose/010) and C/13_L/prose/002 (one of four branches does not have the property).
